messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridian.ai>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO qualification — Veridian Analytics

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to make sure we're aligned on SLOs and the cost/perf levers we'll evaluate during the pilot.

Recap (from our discussion)
- Product: interactive summarization and conversational insights (streaming partial responses)
- Target SLOs: p50 ~150ms, p95 <= 400ms end-to-end for user-facing token delivery (streaming enabled)
- Expected peak throughput: ~120 qps; sustained baseline ~30 qps
- Target concurrency: ~20 simultaneous users / sessions
- Typical request size: short prompts (avg 120 tokens), occasional long context up to 1k tokens

Primary constraints you mentioned
- Streaming required for UX (partial token flush important)
- Low tolerance for quality regressions on hallucination-sensitive flows
- Data controls: PII redaction on ingest; 90-day logs retention preferred

Cost/perf levers we'll consider during qualification
- Continuous batching: reduces per-token cost at high qps while meeting latency SLOs for many requests
- KV/prefix caching: saves compute for repeated system prompts / shared prefixes
- Quantization profiles: 4-bit/INT4 for aggressive cost reduction, evaluate quality delta vs 8-bit/FP16 fallbacks
- Model variants: 7B-quantized for low-latency baseline; 13B or 34B variants for higher quality routes (can route by customer tier or route on fallback)
- Streaming-friendly kernels: measure tokenization and chunk delivery latency to understand end-to-end p95 impact

Ask / next steps
1) Can you share a one-day sample traffic trace (timestamps, request size distribution, and a couple of representative prompt examples)? I attached an SLO_calc_template.csv to make the traffic profile easy to fill in.
2) Confirm whether p95 requirement is hard constraint (i.e., must be <=400ms) or a target we can hit 80% of the time during peak with graceful degradation.
3) We'll propose a 2-week pilot: 1 week of profiling + tuning in Redwood Dedicated (or hosted with dedicated pool) + 1 week of small-scale load test. Proposed window: week of Apr 10.

I've attached a quick cost-estimate PDF and the SLO_calc_template. I'll loop in Dylan (infra) and Dev (solutions) on follow-ups.

If that looks right, please reply with the sample trace and any additional constraints (security, retention, redlines).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridian.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — Veridian Analytics

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and I've attached a small sample we exported from our proxy (veridian_traffic_sample.json).

Clarifications:
- SLO: p95 <= 400ms is our target; for a hard SLA we'd want <= 500ms, but we need p95 ~400ms for a good UX. So treat 400ms as our primary target.
- Peak throughput is actually spiky — expect short bursts up to ~180 qps for ~1-2 minute windows during peak usage. Baseline 25-35 qps.
- Concurrency: 20 active sessions is a good working number; behind this we do session multiplexing.
- Streaming: required — we rely on partial tokens for progressive rendering.
- Models: open to quantized variants. Preference to start with a trusted 13B chat model variant for quality, but we can test 7B quantized for latency/cost comparisons.
- Compliance: We need to ensure logs used for debugging are scrubbed for PII; retention configurable to 90 days.

Attached: veridian_traffic_sample.json (anonymized). I'll also get legal to confirm retention controls; they usually sign off quickly when we provide the specific retention config.

Samir
Samir Patel
VP, Engineering — Veridian Analytics
samir.patel@veridian.ai

Great, thanks for the sample and clarifications — that helps a lot. Looping in Dylan (infra) and Dev (solutions) to propose a concrete pilot plan. Outline below and proposed sign-offs.

Pilot plan (proposed)
- Week 1 (Profiling + config): run traffic trace against Redwood test harness to gather latency breakdowns (tokenization, kernel, network, streaming flush). We'll try three configurations:
  1) 13B FP16 baseline (quality-first)
  2) 13B INT8 / 8-bit quantized (balanced)
  3) 7B INT4 quantized + aggressive batching + KV caching (latency/cost-first)
- Week 2 (Small-scale load test): replay 1-2 day traffic sample with synthetic spikes up to 180 qps to verify p95 and cost estimates.

Cost/perf levers we'll instrument and measure
- Continuous batching windows (10-50ms tradeoff sweep) to see per-token cost vs p95 impact
- KV/prefix caching hit rates for your common system prompts; estimate cost savings if hit >40%
- Quantization profile comparison (INT4 vs INT8 vs FP16) with quality eval on your short prompt set
- Model routing policy: keep default route to 13B, fallback to 7B quant for very high concurrency or cost ceilings

Deliverables and timeline
- By Apr 6: Redwood shares an initial runbook and a tuned cost estimate based on your sample (attached sample runbook and pilot MOP).
- Week of Apr 10: run profiling and begin tuning.
- Week of Apr 17: run load test and deliver final SLO compliance report + cost breakdown.

Security / retention note
- We'll ensure logs used for debugging are redacted by default; retention config adjustable to 90 days. We can surface redaction options in the runbook.

Please confirm the pilot window and we'll book the run slots. I've attached the pilot MOP for your review.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: pilot_mop.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Quick technical note from infra side:
- Streaming + continuous batching: we can support streaming while still batching at the micro-window level. In practice we use short batching windows (10-25ms) and stream partial tokens as soon as they're available — this preserves streaming UX while still gaining batching efficiency.
- For the load test, please include a few representative payload shapes: small interactive prompts (<=150 tokens), medium (150-600 tokens), and long (600-1k tokens). Also include a sample of session-based repeated prefixes so we can measure KV cache hit rate.

I'll instrument the kernels and provide token-level timing (kernel, KV fetch, serialization) during the profiling run.

—Dylan
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
